additions.title: ICT Sector Guidance built on the GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard, Chapter 4: Cloud and data center services
additions.locator: Chapter 4, 'Executive Summary: Cloud and data center services', printed page 4-4 (PDF page 120); section 4.6 on allocation
additions.quote: a key question is how to allocate the GHG emissions of a data center to its various services and clients
additions.why: The standard-setter's own method for working out a customer's share of a shared data centre's emissions, which is the problem a buyer of cloud AI faces. Limits: voluntary guidance dated July 2017, written before generative AI; it covers greenhouse gases, not water; it does not mention AI.

additions.title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
additions.publisher: Government Digital Service (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)
additions.locator: Principle 2 'You use AI lawfully, ethically and responsibly'; section 'Using AI safely and responsibly', sustainability bullet and practical recommendations
additions.quote: You should understand and manage the environmental impact of the AI systems you are planning to use.
additions.why: Government's own instruction to its departments: assess the environmental impact before development, weigh it against benefit, and judge suppliers' environmental credentials. It is the nearest UK official statement of what the criterion asks. Limits: guidance for the public sector, not binding on business; gives no measurement method.

additions.title: Water use in AI and Data Centres
additions.publisher: Government Digital Sustainability Alliance (published by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs)
additions.locator: Section 1, introduction (PDF page 2); section on UK regulation and the transparency gap; strategic recommendations
additions.quote: accurate measurement is foundational to targeted intervention and accountability
additions.why: Covers the water side of the footprint for the UK, which the existing list lacks, and says the data to measure it is missing. Limits: written by an industry alliance convened by Defra and published on GOV.UK; it makes recommendations to government rather than stating policy; several figures are taken from secondary sources and were not checked here.

additions.title: Directive (EU) 2023/1791 on energy efficiency (recast), Article 12: Data centres
additions.publisher: European Union (Publications Office copy of the Official Journal text)
additions.locator: Article 12(1) to (4); Annex VII lists the information
additions.quote: to make the information set out in Annex VII publicly available
additions.why: Binding EU rule that operators of data centres of at least 500kW installed IT power demand publish energy and sustainability information each year. It shows what a legal disclosure duty looks like where the UK has none, and is a source of supplier data for UK firms using EU-hosted services. Limits: not UK law; binds member states and operators, not customers; the duty is per data centre, not per AI service; later delegated acts on the rating scheme were not read.

additions.title: The Large and Medium-sized Companies and Groups (Accounts and Reports) Regulations 2008, Schedule 7, Part 7A: energy and carbon report (unquoted companies)
additions.quote: the annual quantity of energy consumed resulting from the purchase of electricity by the company for its own use
additions.why: The binding UK rule behind the brief's statement that energy and carbon reporting covers a company's own energy use: gas, transport fuel and electricity bought for its own use. Energy used by a cloud or AI supplier on the company's behalf is outside it. Limits: applies to large companies only; Part 7A was inserted in 2018; the site notes revised text may not be fully up to date.

additions.title: Making AI Less "Thirsty": Uncovering and Addressing the Secret Water Footprint of AI Models
additions.publisher: Li, Yang, Islam and Ren; arXiv (accepted by Communications of the ACM)
additions.quote: we provide a principled methodology to estimate the water footprint of AI
additions.why: The main research source on AI's water use, with a method for estimating it; the brief keeps water in scope and the log recorded that no method had been read. Limits: arXiv copy of a paper accepted by a peer-reviewed magazine; the 2027 projection is a model estimate; examples drawn from US data centres.

additions.title: Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale
additions.quote: we find the median Gemini Apps text prompt consumes 0.24 Wh of energy
additions.why: A supplier's measured energy, carbon and water per prompt in production, with the measurement boundary stated: the kind of supplier disclosure the criterion's third level relies on. Limits: preprint, not peer reviewed; written by the supplier about its own product; a median for text prompts only; excludes training; not comparable with other suppliers' figures without the same boundary.

brief_check: Nothing read contradicts the brief. One gap, not an error: the brief's EU sentence names only the AI Act; Directive (EU) 2023/1791 Art. 12 separately makes data centres of 500kW or more publish energy information, which is public, unlike the AI Act documentation. The UK position ('no UK law requires...') is consistent with S.I. 2008/410 Sch. 7 para. 20D as read today.
